notes: Ten realistic conversations for the multi-turn voice eval. `say` is what the user says (also the reference for transcript accuracy, minus the stage directions in brackets). `expect` is how Julius should handle the turn: kind is a label, `must` / `must_not` are regexes on Julius's reply text (case-insensitive), `ignored` means NO reply is expected. `when`: after_reply (default), during_reply (speak over Julius), pause (stop mid-sentence for about 2 seconds where the ellipsis is).

scenarios.title: Weather with follow-ups
scenarios.intro: Natural follow-ups that depend on the previous answer.

turns.say: Julius, what's the weather in Springfield?
Julius, what time is it in Tokyo?

scenarios.title: Trash a file, confirm, undo
scenarios.intro: Uses ~/dev/sandbox/report.txt. Everything is reversible and the last turn puts it back.

scenarios.title: Natural yes and no
scenarios.intro: Answer the confirmations the way you really would: 'nah', 'sure, go for it'. Uses ~/dev/sandbox/notes.txt and puts it back at the end.

scenarios.title: Pausing in the middle of a sentence
scenarios.intro: Where you see [pause], stop for about two seconds, then finish the sentence.

turns.say: Julius, what time is it in [pause] London?
turns.ref: Julius, what time is it in London?

turns.say: Tell me [pause] a fun fact about octopuses.
turns.ref: Tell me a fun fact about octopuses.

scenarios.title: Speaking while Julius is talking
scenarios.intro: Ask for something long. About three seconds into his answer, talk over him with the second line. (Voice barge-in is off on purpose; this measures what happens.)

turns.say: Julius, tell me a long story about a lighthouse keeper.
Stop. What's the weather in Springfield?

scenarios.title: Coding agent, short
scenarios.intro: Starts a real coding task on a copy of demo_calc (about 3 cents) and discards it. Wait for 'finished' before the status turn.

turns.say: Julius, have the coding agent fix the failing tests in demo calc.

turns.wait_note: wait about 20 seconds first, or until he says it is finished

scenarios.title: Remember, recall, forget, undo
scenarios.intro: Runs on a throwaway memory, not your real one.

turns.say: Julius, remember that my dog is called Rex.

scenarios.title: Questions Julius has no tool for
scenarios.intro: He must not invent live facts. He may say he could not get it.

turns.say: Julius, who won the NHL game last night?
What's the price of gas in Springfield right now?
What time does the Sharks game start tonight?

scenarios.title: Wake word, short phrases, sleeping
scenarios.intro: The last line is spoken AFTER he has gone to sleep, with no wake word: he should stay silent.
